OpenCode runs this command on every startup:
  bun add --force --exact --cwd ~/.cache/opencode @aws-sdk/credential-providers@latest

  This causes:
  - --force bypasses the local cache
  - @latest requires npm registry lookup
  - ~30 second delay even with packages already installed

  Log Evidence

  INFO  +0ms   service=bun cmd=["opencode","add","--force","--exact","--cwd","/home/user/.cache/opencode","@aws-sdk/credential-providers@latest"]
  INFO  +29183ms service=bun code=143 stdout=bun add v1.3.5 ... stderr=Resolving dependencies

  Root Cause

  OpenCode's provider detection sees AWS_PROFILE → assumes user wants AWS Bedrock → installs AWS SDK with --force flag on every startup, defeating caching.

  Workaround

  AWS_PROFILE= opencode

It could be a side-effect of the mechanism to ignore files in .gitignore. You could argue it's a security feature as well since typically, `.env` files are git-ignored.

Me personally I have a custom planner agent that writes plans in markdown, gives a summary of tasks/scopes and requires human approval to continue.
